The results for sequential edits on GPT-J are shown in Table 2. We indeed find that edits made using r-ROME create more generalized edits at the slight expense of efficacy as in 1 but downstream performance is retained at scale. The original implementation's downstream performance collapses almost immediately (3). p-ROME surprisingly retains downstream performance better than r-ROME at the tail end of the sequential edits. We suspect this is related to the instability and noise the random prefixes induce: r-ROME n-gram entropies are more widely distributed than p-ROME (2). We observe similar trends in the sequential editing scenario with GPT2-XL 1.5B as with GPT-J 6B.
